Enter your text to hash and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Generate the SHA-512 hash of any text. SHA-512 is the strongest member of the SHA-2 family: it turns any input into a fixed 128-character hexadecimal fingerprint, and the same input always produces the same hash, while even a one-character change produces a completely different one. It is used to verify file integrity and sign data where the longest available hash is wanted. The hashing runs in your browser with the Web Crypto API — your text is never uploaded or stored.

## How to use the SHA-512 Hash Generator

Start by typing or pasting your text to hash. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste the text you want to hash.
2. The SHA-512 hash appears instantly, in hexadecimal and in Base64.
3. Copy the hash with the copy button.

## Formula

SHA-512 processes the input in 1024-bit blocks through 80 rounds of mixing, and outputs a 512-bit digest shown as 128 hexadecimal characters. It is a one-way function: you cannot recover the input from the hash.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [SHA-512 Hash Generator](/sha512-hash-generator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

Here is a typical example. The SHA-512 hash of “Hello, world!” is c1527cd893c124773d811911970c8fe6e857d6df5dc9226bd8a160614c0cd963a4ddea2b94bb7d36021ef9d865d5cea294a82dd49a0bb269f51f6e7a57f79421. Change one letter and the hash changes completely. ## What a hash is for

A hash is a fingerprint: it lets you check that data has not changed without storing the data itself. Download a file, hash it, and compare with the hash the publisher lists — if they match, the file is intact. Password systems store hashes (with a unique salt per user) instead of passwords, so a leaked database does not expose the passwords.

## SHA-512 vs SHA-256

SHA-512 is the 512-bit member of the same SHA-2 family as SHA-256. Its longer digest gives a bigger safety margin against future attacks, and on 64-bit computers it is often faster than SHA-256 because it works on 64-bit words. For most purposes the two are interchangeable — SHA-512 is the choice when the longest available hash is wanted, for example in high-security signing and verification.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- The same input always gives the same hash — use that to verify downloads.
- SHA-512 is the strongest SHA-2 hash; SHA-256 is the common default.
- Never use plain SHA-512 to store passwords; use bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2 with a salt.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is SHA-512?

A cryptographic hash function that turns any input into a fixed 512-bit (128 hex character) fingerprint. It is deterministic, one-way, and a tiny change in the input produces a completely different hash. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-512 Hash Generator](/sha512-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between SHA-512 and SHA-256?

SHA-512 produces a 128-character hash and SHA-256 a 64-character one. Both are trusted; SHA-512 gives a bigger safety margin and is often faster on 64-bit computers. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-512 Hash Generator](/sha512-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is SHA-512 secure?

Yes — SHA-512 is a current, trusted hash function with no practical attacks. Short or common inputs are still vulnerable to guessing, which is why passwords need a salt and a slow hash function such as bcrypt or Argon2. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-512 Hash Generator](/sha512-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my text uploaded anywhere?

No. The hashing runs in your browser with the Web Crypto API — the text never leaves your device. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-512 Hash Generator](/sha512-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
